answer: When k coordinated identities equivocate on the same consensus duty, the protocol aggregates attributable bond penalties so the base loss grows as O(k²), rather than treating each identity as an isolated offender. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the swarm’s bonded escrows, making identity splitting costly. Juniper, trellis, and cipher audit labels can help trace correlated evidence; asymmetric depreciation ensures slashed capital is not restored at face value.
